name: Portal Authentication & Authorization + Abuse-Resistance Hardening
description: Andrew-direct 2026-07-20: harden the opalinvest.dev portal auth stack against the realistic attack paths in Andrew's 'Authentication and Authorization Hardening Proposal' (brute-force / credential stuffing / compromised account / cross-tenant access / scraping / serverless cost amplification / infra compromise). MSTR grounded the live stack at source and authored docs/briefs/PORTAL_AUTH_HARDENING_BRIEF_20260720.md. VERDICT: the foundational model is sound and in several dimensions EXCEEDS the proposal's 'as understood' -- the trust boundary is closed at the edge (auth-validator-edge verifies the RS256 JWT and injects server-derived X-Firm-Id/X-User-Role, overwriting client headers) plus advisor-id (004a) + ownership-map account/relationship (004c) + tier-role (ROLGAT) scoping + an explicit cross-firm secret Deny + a FIRMSEP alarm suite. The real GAPS are concentrated on the abuse-resistance + account-lifecycle axis, not tenant-isolation: G1 no login throttle (only a coarse WAF 2000/5min/IP), G2 no MFA for any portal user incl admins, G3 no session revocation and refresh() never re-checks status (a disabled user keeps minting tokens for the 7-day refresh window), G4 the FIRMSEP alarms fire into an SNS topic with NO subscriber (pages nobody) + zero auth-abuse alarms, G5 a shared authorizer role + secret:opal/* wildcards, G6 no per-user/cost extraction controls, G7 password min-8-not-12, G8 [CONFIRM] direct-to-origin bypass of the edge scoping gates. DynamoDB-not-SQL, so the proposal's SQL-injection/row-level-security items transform to DynamoDB key-condition + IAM LeadingKeys defense-in-depth. Eight workstreams WS-1..8 in the brief S4.
